verdict.root_cause: At 08:33:59Z an automated actor (platform-automation) lowered the container memory limit on frauddetection-service to 200m (tr_91f6abb9990d). Within about a minute the service stopped emitting its steady-state Kafka order-consumption lines and entered a sustained crash/restart loop: the JVM/agent startup triple repeats on a near-constant ~62s cadence from 08:35 through at least 08:42, with no application ERROR or exception text at any point, including around the 08:40 alert (tr_48f2dfb41dd7). A process killed by the kernel for exceeding its cgroup limit dies without emitting an application-level error, which matches exactly what the logs show. The absence of any calls_total series — numerator and denominator both empty — over 08:30–08:45 (tr_6a4a801562db, tr_897542911029) is the metrics-side shadow of the same fact: the container never lives long enough past agent attach to serve traffic or export span metrics. The most probable root cause is a self-inflicted resource-limit reduction that put the ceiling below the JVM's configured/committed footprint, causing repeated kills before application readiness.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on one timeline. (1) Change: exactly one change landed in the window and it is a resource-limit reduction, six minutes before the incident marker; code deploy, feature flag, and dependency bump were each explicitly ruled out from the same change history (tr_91f6abb9990d). (2) Logs: the transition from normal order-consumption output at 08:30 to eight regularly-spaced startup cycles between 08:35 and 08:42 is a restart loop, not a deploy or one-off restart, and the specialist ruled out both a broken log pipeline and a failed agent attach as explanations for the missing error text (tr_48f2dfb41dd7). The failure occurring after agent attach but before any application logging places the kill in the early-heap-growth phase, which is where a too-low memory ceiling bites. (3) Metrics: the empty calls_total denominator rules out the 'healthy service, mild error fraction' reading and is consistent with a process that never reaches serving state (tr_6a4a801562db, tr_897542911029). No single dispatch proves OOM; the confidence rests on the timing coincidence plus the specific signature of silent, periodic death. Remediation is a config revert rather than a rollback because no code artifact changed — only the ceiling — and the actor is an automation controller, so the revert may need to be applied at the policy level or it will be re-applied.
open_questions: No container memory telemetry was ever retrieved. container_memory_working_set_bytes, container_spec_memory_limit_bytes, an OOM-kill counter, or a kube-state-metrics restart count would confirm or refute the OOM hypothesis directly; both metrics dispatches ran only an error-ratio query and explicitly left this open (tr_897542911029).

The prior memory limit is not recorded (tr_91f6abb9990d), so the magnitude of the reduction is unknown and it cannot be shown that 200m is actually below the JVM's configured heap plus overhead. A JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS / -Xmx value would settle whether 200m is genuinely insufficient.

Why platform-automation made this change is unknown — a limit-tuning controller, a policy rollout, or a bad admission-webhook default would each imply different scope. Other services may have received the same reduction; triage covered only frauddetectionservice.

The empty calls_total series has a second candidate explanation the specialists flagged but did not eliminate: a label/metric-name mismatch or absent spanmetrics pipeline for this service (tr_6a4a801562db). If that is the case, the metrics evidence corroborates nothing and the verdict rests on change timing plus logs alone.
Downstream impact is unmeasured. Order consumption stopped by 08:35 with a counter at 388; whether Kafka lag, unprocessed orders, or dependent services degraded was not investigated.
